[To [Anne](../persons.html#1582)] I am going to Hursley to-day to stay with [Mr.

Keble](../persons.html#798), in the hopes of hastening the departure of this tiresome cold.[^1] I like the thought of the visit very much, though it being the first time of my staying out by myself, how I shall manage winding up my watch remains to be proved.

[^1]: ‘A lingering cough, in the spring of 1839, led to my spending a fortnight at the Vicarage; and this rendered it altogether another home, where for twenty-seven years every joy and care were alike carried to those who could “make grief less bitter, joy less wild.”‘ [Musings over the Christian Year](../books.html#88), vi. (The quotation is from a poem which CMY made the epigraph to [The Daisy Chain](../books.html#24), Chapter 14: and described there as ‘Lines on a Monument at Lichfield’.)
